stance_text: Watch — unchanged, bias now negative; value lowered because 2026 earnings are tracking well below the consensus the prior call leaned on, and the price sits almost exactly on our value
lens_text: FY2029 company-adjusted diluted EPS x P/E, from hold-normalized FY2026 EPS (each property at its own 2024-2025 average hold; Wynn Macau VIP at its stated range); three-year value, undiscounted, dividends excluded

bear.basis: Flat property EBITDAR from about $2.1B hold-normalized; depreciation -$0.45, net interest -$0.25, Al Marjan -$0.20; no net buyback: FY2029 adjusted EPS $2.88 x 13x

base.basis: Property EBITDAR +3% a year (+$195M, about +$1.46); depreciation -$0.45, net interest -$0.15, Al Marjan +$0.65 (about $550M EBITDA at 100%, our estimate); 3% fewer shares: FY2029 adjusted EPS $5.45 x 16x

bull.basis: Property EBITDAR +5% a year (+$331M); depreciation -$0.45, net interest -$0.10, Al Marjan +$1.55 (about $800M EBITDA at 100%); 4% fewer shares: FY2029 adjusted EPS $7.57 x 19x

horizon_text: End-2029 value on FY2029 adjusted EPS, undiscounted
thesis: Q3 adjusted EPS fell to $0.33 from $0.86 as EBITDAR dropped at every property, and nine-month EPS of $2.83 puts FY2026 near $3.83, about 19% below the $4.70 consensus the September call used. Wynn Palace's 27.4% nine-month mass hold flattered the year, but low hold in Las Vegas, Boston and at Wynn Macau offset most of it; normalized FY2026 EPS is about $3.78. At $87.30 the stock is 22.8x this year's earnings, against 16.2x for Las Vegas Sands, while about $1.95 billion is due or puttable in 2027 and Al Marjan and the Enclave absorb cash. If property EBITDAR grows 3% a year and Al Marjan earns about $0.65 a share by 2029, the stock is worth about $87, today's price.
consensus_view: No Street snapshot was captured. In August the consensus had $4.70 of FY2026 and $5.16 of FY2027 adjusted EPS; Q3 makes the 2026 figure unreachable. The stock fell to $71.38 in late October and has recovered to $87.30, 22.8x our FY2026 estimate and about 17x the August FY2027 consensus, as if 2027 earnings will recover to consensus.
variant_view: The market looks through 2026 to a recovery near the August FY2027 consensus of $5.16. We think 2027 comes in lower: Palace's mass drop fell 12.9% in Q3 and its hold has run above its own history, Al Marjan contributes nothing to 2027 earnings before a September opening, and refinancing adds interest. We expect FY2027 adjusted EPS below $5.00, which leaves the stock fairly valued rather than cheap.

Revised twice after independent review (C, then B). The first revision normalized Macau hold to its own history and rated Avoid at -0.6% a year; the second applied the same yardstick to Las Vegas and Boston and corrected the convertible's interest effect, giving $88.92 (+0.6% a year) and Watch. First-round counter-case argued Avoid; see review for the second.

First review round (C; evidence 3, valuation 3, variant view 2, risk 3, calibration 4): hold benchmarks were inconsistent, the bridge left out refinancing interest, the 17x base exit sat above both peers, consensus_view misstated the P/E as 16x, and a kill criterion would fire on hold alone.

low_score_reasons: evidence: the drivers that decide the sign (flow-throughs, $0.75 per $100M, depreciation step-up, Al Marjan EBITDA, the interest line) are unsourced; the redeemed 2027 notes were $880.0M in the 10-Q, not $900M; the workbook Fundamentals sheet carried the FY2018 revenue.

valuation: fair value sat $1.60 below price and a 17x base exit, no hold adjustment, Las Vegas and Boston at their own two-year averages (the Macau yardstick), or the September weights each restore Watch; the bridge counted the convertible put as adding interest when repaying it removes about $50M a year.
variant_view: 'the market prices 2027 near the August consensus' is inferred from a multiple with no snapshot; the FY2026 below-$4.00 claim is nearly arithmetic.

risk: the Al Marjan kill criterion tested the remaining contribution, which falls as Wynn pays in, so it would fire mechanically; criterion 1 could fire on hold luck; $750M of 2027 Wynn Macau notes and a $600M 2027 retail term loan were left out.
review.counter_case: Watch: FY2026 is a trough year (Q3 Las Vegas hold 18.9%, a Boston strike, Macau drop down), and the base case only needs FY2029 EPS of $5.25 on 3% growth (43rd percentile), still below the $6.02 Wynn earned in FY2024. The Avoid sat $1.60 below price and turns positive with a 17x base exit, no hold adjustment, Las Vegas and Boston held to their own two-year averages like Macau, or the September weights. The interest drag partly counted the convertible put the wrong way, and the $1.00 dividend and up to $268M of buybacks below $90 make expected total return positive. A rating that one defensible input moves across the line is a hold, not a sell.
review.response: Accepted, and the stance returns to Watch with a negative bias. Every property is now normalized to its own 2024-2025 average hold (Las Vegas 24.75%, Boston 20.6%, Palace 23.65%, Wynn Macau 18.1%; Wynn Macau VIP to its stated range), for -$0.05 over nine months and $3.78 of normalized FY2026 EPS. Net interest is -$0.25/-$0.15/-$0.10, counting the $15.7M a year of the 2035 refinancing ($880M redeemed) and the convertible's roughly $50M of interest as a saving if repaid. Values are $37.44 / $87.20 / $143.83 and fair value $88.92 (+0.6% a year). The Al Marjan kill criterion now tests the total commitment ($1.71B), the EPS criterion requires normal hold, and the 2027 obligations (about $1.95B) are in the note and pre-mortem. The 16x base exit stays, since it is a premium to Sands on GAAP earnings; the note states that 30/50/20 weights or a 15x exit would rate Avoid. The workbook's Fundamentals sheet is generated from SEC facts; the stale FY2018 revenue there is a tool issue logged for a fix, and inputs.json carries the correct $7,268.7M.
